priorStories.headline: Brewers win their first World Series
priorStories.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5, securing the first World Series championship in the franchise’s history.

Jacob Misiorowski pitched 5 2/3 scoreless innings, and Cooper Pratt had two hits and two RBIs. Catcher William Contreras was named the series’ most valuable player.

priorStories.headline: Judge lets California process up to 20,000 ballots
priorStories.body:
A federal judge denied the Justice Department’s request to stop California from processing ballots from as many as 20,000 people the government alleged were likely noncitizens.

Judge David O. Carter said segregating the ballots could disenfranchise eligible voters and disrupt an election already underway. California can continue processing them while the litigation proceeds. The Justice Department said it would appeal.

priorStories.headline: Federal Reserve leaves interest rates unchanged
priorStories.body:
The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark federal funds rate at 3.75% to 4%, leaving the rate unchanged as officials described economic activity as strong and inflation as still elevated.

The decision passed 10-2. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack favored raising the range by a quarter percentage point.

priorStories.headline: Spain train collision kills at least 68
priorStories.body:
At least 68 people were reported dead and dozens injured after two high-speed trains collided near Urda in Spain’s Toledo province.

One train struck the rear of another that had stopped, derailing two cars. Rescue and investigative work continued, and rail service remained disrupted on affected routes.

candidates.summary: The Bureau of Economic Analysis estimated that real U.S. gross domestic product grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter, up from 2.2% in the second quarter. A separate BEA release said September's PCE price index rose 0.5% from August and 3.6% from a year earlier; excluding food and energy, it rose 0.3% monthly and 3.1% annually. Both are initial estimates subject to revision.
candidates.title: U.S. economy grows at 3.4% annual rate in third quarter

candidates.summary: Initial applications for U.S. unemployment benefits fell to 194,000 for the latest reported week from a revised 195,000. The four-week average declined to 196,750, and weekly claims remained at or below 200,000 for a seventh consecutive week.
candidates.title: U.S. initial jobless claims fall to 194,000

candidates.summary: Iran's state broadcaster, citing the Revolutionary Guard, said three oil tankers struck mines and caught fire while trying to leave the Strait of Hormuz through a restricted route during the preceding 24 hours. The vessels were not identified, and casualties were not reported. The Associated Press could not independently confirm the account; a British maritime monitor separately reported seeing one vessel on fire in the strait.
candidates.title: Iran says three tankers struck mines in Strait of Hormuz

candidates.summary: The Houthi-run Health Ministry said a strike on two homes in Taiz, Yemen, killed 12 people and critically wounded three others, including women and children. The ministry blamed Saudi Arabia. The Associated Press said it could not independently verify the report.
candidates.title: Houthis say strike in Taiz killed 12 people

candidates.summary: Health officials at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital said an Israeli strike on a civilian vehicle in central Gaza killed two people and wounded one. Israel's military had not responded to the Associated Press's request for comment at the time of reporting.
candidates.title: Hospital officials say Israeli strike killed two in Gaza

candidates.summary: The United States and Finland signed a nonbinding memorandum to expand cooperation on artificial intelligence, telecommunications, quantum technology, energy, semiconductors, space, biotechnology, research security, shipbuilding and Arctic technology. The document does not itself commit either government to spend funds or create legally binding obligations.
candidates.title: United States and Finland sign technology cooperation memorandum

candidates.summary: The Houthi-run Health Ministry said a Saudi airstrike in western Taiz province killed at least 13 people, mostly women and children. The Saudi-led coalition did not immediately comment.
candidates.title: Houthis say Saudi airstrike in Taiz killed 13 people

candidates.summary: Israel's completed election count gave Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats, the main opposition 48 and Arab-led parties 19. No bloc secured the 61 seats needed for a majority. The results remained subject to certification and submission to President Isaac Herzog.
candidates.title: Israeli election count leaves no bloc with a majority

candidates.summary: Chief U.S. District Judge James Boasberg ordered the Trump administration to identify by Friday all states whose election officials received Justice Department demands concerning alleged noncitizen voters. Boasberg said he intended to rule by Monday on Democratic organizations' request to restrict federal intervention in state election procedures.
candidates.title: Judge orders disclosure of federal noncitizen-voter inquiries

candidates.summary: U.S. District Judge David O. Carter appointed Daniel B. Garrie as special master to develop the factual record concerning the federal government's list of roughly 20,000 California voters it alleges are likely noncitizens. Carter scheduled a November 13 evidentiary hearing while allowing ballot processing to continue.
candidates.title: Judge appoints special master to examine California voter claims

candidates.summary: The U.S. Energy Department awarded contracts to exchange more than 40 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The department said the awards completed a planned 172-million-barrel emergency release and require more than 216 million barrels to be returned to the reserve beginning in 2027.
candidates.title: Energy Department awards contracts for 40 million barrels of reserve oil

candidates.summary: North Korean state media said Kim Jong Un visited an exhibition of attack and other drones and called for rapid expansion of unmanned-aircraft technology. It said North Korea also tested drones, missiles and large-caliber multiple rocket launchers. Independent journalists were not given access to the exhibition or tests.
candidates.title: North Korea displays drones and conducts weapons tests
